Broken glass

Broken Side and Rear Glass: Cleanup, Interior Repair and Coordination

Replacement glass is installed by our third-party glass partner. The glass that exploded into your seats, carpet, vents and door is still your problem, and so is the interior and paint damage around the break. That part is ours.

What we do when a window is broken

  • Deep glass removal: tempered side and rear glass breaks into thousands of pieces that end up under seats, inside door panels, in vents and defroster ducts. We remove trim and seats as needed and clean those cavities out.
  • Interior repair: cut or scuffed seats, scratched panels, a dumped console, footprints and spills from the break-in.
  • Paint around the opening: scratches and scuffs on the door frame or quarter panel from the break or the tool used.
  • Weather protection: we can secure the opening with a temporary cover while the replacement glass is on the way.
  • Coordination: we coordinate the replacement glass through our glass partner and schedule the cleanup around the installation, so the interior is clean before the new glass goes in.

What we are honest about

We are a detail and restoration shop; we do not stock or install glass ourselves. We coordinate glass replacement through our third-party glass partner and handle the related cleanup and restoration. If your insurer arranges an installer through its own glass network, we are glad to work alongside them instead.

Windshields: windshield chips and cracks are an installer’s job and often a separate glass-coverage claim. We do not repair windshields.

What to do right now

  1. If it was a break-in, file a police report and photograph the vehicle before touching anything.
  2. Cover the opening with plastic and tape so rain and more debris stay out.
  3. Contact your insurer to open or discuss the claim, and send us photos — we coordinate the replacement glass through our glass partner and schedule the cleanup and interior repair around it.

Glass, cleanup and your insurance

Broken glass from a break-in or vandalism is typically part of a comprehensive claim, and some policies carry separate glass coverage with its own deductible. The interior cleanup and repair that goes with a break-in is usually part of the same claim, and we itemize it so your insurer can see exactly what was done and why. Coverage, and what your deductible is, are always your insurance company’s decision, never ours.

Contact your insurer to open or discuss a claim; we provide an itemized, written estimate and damage documentation, and we coordinate the repair process once you decide to proceed.

Questions people ask

Do you replace car windows?

Not in-house. We coordinate glass replacement through our third-party glass partner, remove the broken glass from the interior and repair the damage the break caused. If your insurer arranges its own installer, we work alongside them.

Why not just vacuum the glass myself?

You can get the big pieces, but tempered glass spreads into seat tracks, door panels, vents and under the carpet, and a household vacuum will not survive it. Fragments left behind come out of the vents for months and cut hands and upholstery.

Should the cleanup happen before or after the new glass?

Before is better, so the installer is not sealing new glass over a dirty channel and nothing gets trapped behind the new trim. We schedule the cleanup around the glass installation.

Will insurance pay for the cleanup?

When the glass broke in a covered event such as a break-in, the related interior cleanup and repair is usually part of the same claim, but your insurer decides. Our itemized estimate explains each line so your insurer can see what was needed.
